en: Theravāda Vinaya Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga Pācittiyakaṇḍa
Ārāmavagga 60.
The Training Rule on Being Born Between the Thighs.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was staying at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, a certain bhikkhunī had a boil growing in her groin, which she had a man drain by himself in a secluded place.
Then that man attempted to violate the bhikkhunī.
She raised a cry.
The bhikkhunīs ran up to that bhikkhunī and said to her,
“Venerable lady, why did you let out a cry?
Then that bhikkhunī explained the matter to the bhikkhunīs.

Those bhikkhunīs who were few in desires … [as before] … complained, grumbled, and spread it about, saying: “How can a bhikkhunī have a boil growing on her private parts lanced by one person alone in “It is true, Blessed One.
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them:
“… How indeed, monks, can a bhikkhunī have a boil growing in her private parts lanced by a man, one-on-one? This is not for the benefit of the bhikkhunīs…”
“Monks, this does not lead to the confidence of those without confidence … [as before] … And so,
monks, the nuns should recite this training rule: ‘Whatever nun,
without having obtained permission from the Saṅgha or a group, [treats] a boil or a wound that has arisen in the groin …’”
Or if she should, together with a man, have one person alone cause another to break [her fast], or cause her to plow, or cause her to wash,
or cause her to anoint, or cause her to bind, or cause her to release, it is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
“Whoever,” however, means:
Whichever [nun] of such a kind...
"a bhikkhunī"...
this is the bhikkhunī intended in this context.
The "thigh" (pasākha) refers to the area below the navel and above the kneecaps. It is called "born" (jāta).
"Produced therein":
a "boil" (gaṇḍa) refers to any kind of boil whatsoever.
"Rudhita" means any kind of wound.
"Without having asked for permission" means:
"Without having asked for permission.
"The Saṅgha" refers to the community of bhikkhunīs.
A "group" (gaṇa) refers to many bhikkhunīs.
A "man" (purisa) refers to...
A human being, not a *yakkha*, not a *peta*, not an animal; one who is conscious and capable of defiling.
"Together" means in one place.
"Both together" means a man and a bhikkhunī.
If he commands, "Destroy [it]," there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
If it is split, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
If one commands, "Split it," there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
When it has been split, there is an offense of expiation.
If she commands, “Wash it,” there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
When it has been washed, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
If she commands, “Anoint it,” there is an offense of wrong-doing.
There is an offense of expiation (pācittiya) for each stitch.
If she commands, "Bind it," there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
When it is bound, there is an offense of expiation.
If she commands, “Urinate,” there is an offense of wrong-doing.
If she urinates, there is an offense of expiation.
There is no offense—
Having obtained permission, she has it split, or has it cut open, or has it washed, or has it smeared, or has it bound, or has it released;
provided there is some intelligent woman acting as her companion, except in the case of one who is insane.
"For one who is a first offender":
thus ends the tenth training rule.
The sixth chapter, the Chapter on Monasteries, is concluded.
